newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - April 24.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on April 24:

LIMA - A day after commandos burst into the Japanese ambassador's residence and ended a 126-day hostage drama, Peruvians learned that the elaborate and long-rehearsed military operation was carried out with secret tunnels, plastic explosives, clandestine radio transmissions and daring exploits that led to the improbably successful outcome.

LIMA - The Rev. Juan Julio Wicht had just lost his afternoon chess game and thought it was a bad joke when one of his fellow hostages whispered that a rescue attempt was imminent after 126 days as captives in the Japanese ambassador's residence.
WASHINGTON - Franklin Roosevelt, who tried hard to hide his paralysis, would sit in a wheelchair in a new statue that President Clinton proposed adding to the FDR memorial after it is opens May 2.

GRAND FORKS, N.D. - What is strangest about a flood that has settled in for a long stay is the quiet. So it is eerily silent in downtown Grand Forks since its 50,000 residents lost their battle with the Red River and evacuated the city.

WASHINGTON - Former Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole reversed course and endorsed a global treaty outlawing chemical weapons, giving the pact a surprise boost on the eve of a Senate showdown over whether to ratify it.

WASHINGTON - Officials in the Department of Veterans Affairs acknowledged that the federal government could be held liable for medical care and compensation to potentially millions of veterans who used tobacco while on active duty and subsequently became ill from tobacco-linked diseases.
WASHINGTON - A 63-year-old California woman using fertility treatments and a donated egg has given birth to a healthy girl, the oldest known woman to become a mother.
